LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_FIVE.titleEnglish: Open a Moment with 的時候
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_FIVE.learnerPromise: Say what happens during a situation or activity.
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_FIVE.explanation: Put the situation or activity before 的時候. Then say what happens in that moment.

lessonWorld.title: Set the moment
lessonWorld.prompt: The speaker likes going out for sport when the weather is good.
lessonWorld.traditional: 天氣好的時候，我喜歡出去運動。
lessonWorld.simplified: 天气好的时候，我喜欢出去运动。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Tiānqì hǎo de shíhou, wǒ xǐhuān chūqù yùndòng.
lessonWorld.english: When the weather is good, I like to go out for sport.

items.question: When working, I use Chinese — is it 工作時候 or 工作的時候?
items.answer: Keep 的. 的 connects the situation to 時候: 工作的時候.

right.english: When working, speak Chinese.

items.question: When I feel unhappy, I listen to music. Where does 不好 go?
items.answer: Keep the situation together: 心情不好, then 的時候. 的時候 needs the whole situation before it.

right.traditional: 心情不好的時候，聽音樂。
right.simplified: 心情不好的时候，听音乐。
right.pinyin: Xīnqíng bù hǎo de shíhòu, tīng yīnyuè.
right.english: When I feel unhappy, I listen to music.

items.question: I drink water while exercising. Is 運動以後 okay?
items.answer: No. 運動以後 means after exercising. For inside the moment, use 運動的時候.

right.pinyin: Yùndòng de shíhòu, wǒ hē shuǐ.
right.english: When exercising, I drink water.

LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_FOUR.titleEnglish: Mark a Life Experience with 過
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_FOUR.learnerPromise: Talk about experiences you have had, and say you have already done something.
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_FOUR.explanation: Put 過 right after a verb for an experience: something you have done before. V過了 relates the finished action closely to now. Use 沒 + verb + 過 for “have not.”

lessonWorld.title: Add an experience
lessonWorld.prompt: The speaker has seen this film.

items.question: Have you ever tried stinky tofu — 吃了 or 吃過?
items.answer: 吃過. 了 asks about one finished meal. 過 asks whether it ever happened in your life.

right.english: Have you ever tried stinky tofu?

items.question: I have worked at a restaurant. Where does 過 go?
items.answer: Between the two parts of 上班: 上過班. It cannot sit at the end of the whole action.

right.english: I have worked at a restaurant before.

items.question: I have not been to Japan — 不 or 沒 before 去過?
items.answer: 沒. 沒 says the experience never happened. 不 says you refuse or will not do it.

right.english: I have not been to Japan.

text.traditional: 很多台灣人去過日本，因為從台灣到日本不遠。
text.pinyin: Hěnduō Táiwānrén qùguo Rìběn, yīnwèi cóng Táiwān dào Rìběn bù yuǎn.
text.english: Many Taiwanese people have been to Japan, because Japan is not far from Taiwan.
text.simplified: 很多台湾人去过日本，因为从台湾到日本不远。

text.traditional: A：他來過我們家嗎？B：來過，那個時候你不在家。
text.pinyin: A: Tā láiguo wǒmen jiā ma? B: Láiguo, nàge shíhou nǐ bú zài jiā.
text.english: A: Has he been to our home? B: Yes; you were not at home then.
text.simplified: A：他来过我们家吗？B：来过，那个时候你不在家。

text.traditional: A：你吃過臭豆腐嗎？B：我還沒吃過，聽說很特別。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ chīguo chòudòufu ma? B: Wǒ hái méi chīguo, tīngshuō hěn tèbié.
text.english: A: Have you eaten stinky tofu? B: I have not eaten it yet; I hear it is very special.
text.simplified: A：你吃过臭豆腐吗？B：我还没吃过，听说很特别。

text.traditional: A：你要跟我們一起吃午飯嗎？B：我吃過了，你們去吃吧！
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ yào gēn wǒmen yìqǐ chī wǔfàn ma? B: Wǒ chīguo le, nǐmen qù chī ba!
text.english: A: Do you want to eat lunch with us? B: I have already eaten; you go eat.
text.simplified: A：你要跟我们一起吃午饭吗？B：我吃过了，你们去吃吧！

text.traditional: A：李小姐今天要來我們公司，她來過了嗎？B：她來過了，是早上來的。
text.pinyin: A: Lǐ xiǎojiě jīntiān yào lái wǒmen gōngsī, tā láiguo le ma? B: Tā láiguo le, shì zǎoshang lái de.
text.english: A: Miss Li is coming to our company today. Has she been here? B: She has; she came in the morning.
text.simplified: A：李小姐今天要来我们公司，她来过了吗？B：她来过了，是早上来的。

text.traditional: A：他給大家寫了一張卡片，你們都看過了嗎？B：我看過了。C：我還沒看。
text.pinyin: A: Tā gěi dàjiā xiě le yì zhāng kǎpiàn, nǐmen dōu kànguo le ma? B: Wǒ kànguo le. C: Wǒ hái méi kàn.
text.english: A: He wrote a card for everyone. Have you all seen it? B: I have. C: I have not yet.
text.simplified: A：他给大家写了一张卡片，你们都看过了吗？B：我看过了。C：我还没看。

LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_ONE.lessonTitleEnglish: What Job Do You Want to Do?
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_ONE.learnerPromise: Name the tool, language, or method you use.
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_ONE.explanation: Put 用 before the tool, language, or method. Say the action after it.

lessonWorld.title: Name your tool
lessonWorld.prompt: The speaker likes writing letters in Chinese.
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān yòng Zhōngwén xiě xìn.
lessonWorld.english: I like to write letters in Chinese.

patternRows.english: I like to write letters in Chinese.
They often use the school internet to get online.

items.question: I write letters using Chinese. Where does 中文 go?
items.answer: 中文 is the tool, so it goes right after 用, before the action: 用中文寫信.

right.english: I write letters using Chinese.

items.question: Can you write with a brush — do I still need 用?
items.answer: Yes. 用 stays between 會 and the tool: 會用毛筆寫字. English drops the word “use”; Chinese does not.

right.pinyin: Nǐ huì yòng máobǐ xiě zì ma?
right.english: Can you write characters with a brush?

items.question: I chat with friends in Chinese — 用 or 跟 before 中文?
items.answer: 用. 用 names the language or tool. 跟 is for the person you do it with: 跟朋友.

right.pinyin: Wǒ yòng Zhōngwén gēn péngyǒu liáotiān.
right.english: I chat with friends in Chinese.

text.traditional: A：你會用毛筆寫字嗎？B：不會，你可以教我嗎？
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ huì yòng máobǐ xiě zì ma? B: Bù huì, nǐ kěyǐ jiāo wǒ ma?
text.english: A: Can you write characters with a brush? B: No. Can you teach me?
text.simplified: A：你会用毛笔写字吗？B：不会，你可以教我吗？

text.traditional: A：你有照相機嗎？B：沒有，我都用手機照相。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ yǒu zhàoxiàngjī ma? B: Méiyǒu, wǒ dōu yòng shǒujī zhàoxiàng.
text.english: A: Do you have a camera? B: No; I always use my phone to take photos.
text.simplified: A：你有照相机吗？B：没有，我都用手机照相。

text.traditional: A：我覺得你中文進步了。B：真的嗎？可能是因為最近我常常用中文跟朋友聊天。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒ juéde nǐ Zhōngwén jìnbù le. B: Zhēnde ma? Kěnéng shì yīnwèi zuìjìn wǒ chángcháng yòng Zhōngwén gēn péngyǒu liáotiān.
text.english: A: I think your Chinese has improved. B: Really? Maybe because I often chat with friends in Chinese recently.
text.simplified: A：我觉得你中文进步了。B：真的吗？可能是因为最近我常常用中文跟朋友聊天。

LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_THREE.titleEnglish: Show an Attitude or Effect with 對
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_THREE.learnerPromise: Say who you speak to, what is good or bad for something, and how someone treats another person.
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_THREE.explanation: 對 points toward a person or thing. Use it for the person you speak to, for something that is good or bad for a target, and for how someone treats another person.

lessonWorld.title: Point the attitude
lessonWorld.prompt: He treats me well and often helps me.
lessonWorld.traditional: 他對我很好，常常幫我忙。
lessonWorld.simplified: 他对我很好，常常帮我忙。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Tā duì wǒ hěn hǎo, chángcháng bāng wǒ máng.
lessonWorld.english: He treats me very well and often helps me.

items.question: The boss is kind to me. Why does 我 come so early?
items.answer: 對 points at the receiver, so 我 follows it right away: 對我好. English puts “to me” at the end; Chinese does not.

right.english: The boss is kind to me.

items.question: My coworkers are kind to me. Did I say it right with 我對同事很好?
items.answer: No — you turned the arrow around. The person right after 對 receives the kindness, so it is 同事對我很好.

right.english: My coworkers are kind to me.

items.question: Phones are bad for my eyes — 對 or 跟 before 眼睛?
items.answer: 對. 對 shows where the effect lands. 跟 is for doing something together with someone.

right.english: Phones are bad for the eyes.

text.traditional: 他常對我說：「我們應該要多運動、多喝水。」
text.pinyin: Tā cháng duì wǒ shuō: “Wǒmen yīnggāi yào duō yùndòng, duō hē shuǐ.”
text.english: He often says to me: “We should exercise more and drink more water.”
text.simplified: 他常对我说：「我们应该要多运动、多喝水。」

text.traditional: 這件事我只對你說，你不要告訴別人。
text.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ zhǐ duì nǐ shuō, nǐ bú yào gàosù biérén.
text.english: I am telling this only to you; do not tell anyone else.
text.simplified: 这件事我只对你说，你不要告诉别人。

text.traditional: 常用手機對眼睛不好。
text.pinyin: Cháng yòng shǒujī duì yǎnjīng bù hǎo.
text.english: Using a phone often is bad for the eyes.
text.simplified: 常用手机对眼睛不好。

text.traditional: 這本書對我不難，我可以學學看。
text.pinyin: Zhè běn shū duì wǒ bù nán, wǒ kěyǐ xuéxue kàn.
text.english: This book is not difficult for me; I can try studying it.
text.simplified: 这本书对我不难，我可以学学看。

text.traditional: 他對我很好，常常幫我忙。
text.pinyin: Tā duì wǒ hěn hǎo, chángcháng bāng wǒ máng.
text.english: He treats me very well and often helps me.
text.simplified: 他对我很好，常常帮我忙。

text.traditional: A：老闆對你們怎麼樣？B：他對我們很不錯，常常要我們多注意身體健康。
text.pinyin: A: Lǎobǎn duì nǐmen zěnmeyàng? B: Tā duì wǒmen hěn búcuò, chángcháng yào wǒmen duō zhùyì shēntǐ jiànkāng.
text.english: A: How does the boss treat you? B: He treats us quite well and often tells us to pay more attention to our health.
text.simplified: A：老板对你们怎么样？B：他对我们很不错，常常要我们多注意身体健康。

LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_TWO.titleEnglish: Place 以前 and 以後 on the Timeline
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_TWO.learnerPromise: Say whether something happened before or will happen after a time or activity.
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_TWO.explanation: 以前 means “before” or “in the past”; 以後 means “after” or “in the future.” Use them alone or right after a time or an activity.

lessonWorld.title: Place the time
lessonWorld.prompt: The speaker was fat before and has lost weight now.

lessonWorld.english: I was fat before; now I have lost several kilograms.

LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_TWO.pattern: Time or Activity + 以前／以後 + Statement

items.question: I go home before three. Where does 以前 go?
items.answer: Right after the time: 三點以前. 我以前三點回家 means something else — “I used to go home at three.”

right.pinyin: Wǒ sān diǎn yǐqián huí jiā.
right.english: I go home before three.

items.question: I want to be a reporter after graduating. Where does 以後 go?
items.answer: Right after the event: 畢業以後. Put it before the event and 以後畢業 means “graduate later.”

right.english: After graduating, I will become a reporter.

items.question: I want to be a reporter someday. Is 半年以後 okay?
items.answer: No. 半年以後 means “six months from now.” For a someday plan, use plain 以後.

right.english: I will become a reporter someday.

text.traditional: 我以前很胖，現在瘦了幾公斤。
text.simplified: 我以前很胖，现在瘦了几公斤。

text.english: I used to be very heavy; now I have lost several kilograms.

text.english: Before, I wanted to work at a bank; now I think being a reporter is not bad either.

text.traditional: 如果你不能來，請你這個禮拜三以前告訴我。
text.simplified: 如果你不能来，请你这个礼拜三以前告诉我。
text.pinyin: Rúguǒ nǐ bù néng lái, qǐng nǐ zhège lǐbàisān yǐqián gàosù wǒ.
text.english: If you cannot come, please tell me before this Wednesday.

items.question: Have you ever tried stinky tofu — 吃了 or 吃過?
items.answer: 吃過. 了 asks about one finished meal. 過 asks whether it ever happened in your life.

items.question: I have worked at a restaurant. Where does 過 go?
items.answer: Between the two parts of 上班: 上過班. It cannot sit at the end of the whole action.

items.question: I have not been to Japan — 不 or 沒 before 去過?

items.question: When working, I use Chinese — is it 工作時候 or 工作的時候?
items.answer: Keep 的. 的 connects the situation to 時候: 工作的時候.

items.question: When I feel unhappy, I listen to music. Where does 不好 go?
items.answer: Keep the situation together: 心情不好, then 的時候. 的時候 needs the whole situation before it.

right.english: When I feel unhappy, I listen to music.

items.question: I drink water while exercising. Is 運動以後 okay?
items.answer: No. 運動以後 means after exercising. For inside the moment, use 運動的時候.

right.pinyin: Yùndòng de shíhòu, wǒ hē shuǐ.
right.english: When exercising, I drink water.

text.traditional: 這樣你在學校的成績，不會有問題嗎？
